title: Continuous $\mathbf Z_\ell$-characters are compatible finite-level classes
statement:
Let $k_0$ be a finite field and let $\ell$ be a prime with $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$, as fixed throughout the chapter. Let $U_0/k_0$ be geometrically connected and separated of finite type,
put $U=U_0\times_{k_0}\overline{k}_0$, and choose a geometric point
$\bar u\to U$. Put $A_n=\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$. There is a
natural Frobenius-equivariant isomorphism

$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(\pi_1(U,\bar u),\mathbf Z_\ell)
\xrightarrow{\sim}
\varprojlim_n H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(U,A_n).
\tag{3.2}
$$

Under the Weil-group action determined by a
degree-one lift $s$, Frobenius on the left is

$$
f\longmapsto\bigl[g\longmapsto f(s^{-1}gs)\bigr].
$$

The cohomology and Weil-group conventions are those of
[def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology], [def-wf-weil-group].
The $\ell$-adic integers carry the valuation topology of [def-weil-l-adic-numbers].

proof.text: Put $\Pi=\pi_1(U,\bar u)$ and give $A_n$ its discrete topology. For every $n\geq1$, [lem-wf-finite-constant-h1-pi1] gives the natural group isomorphism $\theta_n:H^1_{\mathrm{\acute et}}(U,A_n)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm{cont}}(\Pi,A_n)$. Apply its naturality to the coefficient homomorphism $c_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n$: $\theta_n(c_{n,*}x)=c_n\circ\theta_{n+1}(x)$. Thus taking $\theta_n$ coordinatewise identifies the inverse limit in the assertion with the group of families $(f_n)$ of continuous homomorphisms satisfying $c_n\circ f_{n+1}=f_n$. The inverse sends $(f_n)$ to $(\theta_n^{-1}f_n)$; the displayed identity verifies its compatibility as well.

Write $\rho_n:\mathbf Z_\ell\to A_n$ for residue. To make pointwise lifting precise, let $R$ be the ring of tuples $(a_n)_{n\geq0}$ with $a_n\in\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z$ and compatible reductions; its operations are coordinatewise. The coordinate projections are unital ring homomorphisms and their compatibility is part of the definition of $R$. Apply [lem-exc-padic-residue-universal-property] to these projections to obtain a unital ring homomorphism $L:R\to\mathbf Z_\ell$ with $\rho_n(L(a))=a_n$. The same node says that residues separate points. Consequently $L((\rho_n(z))_n)=z$, whereas $(\rho_n(L(a)))_n=a$. In particular every compatible tuple has one and only one lift. The $n=0$ coordinate is the unique element of $\mathbf Z/1\mathbf Z$, so adjoining or forgetting it changes no compatible family indexed by $n\geq1$.

source.place: Proof, the pointwise identification of the residue limit with the adic integers

proof.text: The kernel and norm clauses of [lem-exc-padic-residue-universal-property] imply that $|x-y|_\ell<\ell^{-n}$ forces $\rho_n(x)=\rho_n(y)$. Therefore $\rho_n$ is locally constant and hence continuous to discrete $A_n$. Given a continuous homomorphism $b:\Pi\to\mathbf Z_\ell$, set $f_n=\rho_n\circ b$. These are continuous homomorphisms. Residue compatibility in the same node gives $c_n\circ f_{n+1}=f_n$. Applying the inverse of the coordinatewise identification in step 1 defines the claimed map $b\mapsto(\theta_n^{-1}(\rho_n\circ b))_n$.

source.place: Proof, reduction of a continuous adic character

proof.text: Conversely, let $(f_n)$ be a compatible family from step 1. For $g\in\Pi$, define $b(g)=L((f_n(g))_n)$ using step 2. Each $f_n$ is a homomorphism, so $f_n(gh)=f_n(g)+f_n(h)$ and $f_n(1)=0$; either coordinatewise addition followed by the ring homomorphism $L$, or residue separation in [lem-exc-padic-residue-universal-property], gives $b(gh)=b(g)+b(h)$ and $b(1)=0$. To check continuity at an arbitrary $g_0$, fix $\varepsilon>0$ and choose $n\geq1$ with $\ell^{-n}<\varepsilon$. The set $V=f_n^{-1}(\{f_n(g_0)\})$ is an open neighbourhood of $g_0$. For $g\in V$, $\rho_n(b(g)-b(g_0))=0$, so the kernel and norm clauses of that node give $|b(g)-b(g_0)|_\ell\leq\ell^{-n}<\varepsilon$. This proves continuity everywhere, without assuming the source group discrete or finite.

source.place: Proof, construction and continuity of the lifted character

proof.text: The two constructions are inverse: starting with $b$, the lifted character has exactly the residues of $b$ at every $g$, hence equals $b$ by [lem-exc-padic-residue-universal-property]; starting with $(f_n)$, the defining property of $L$ recovers each $f_n$. The map is additive because residue maps and the group isomorphisms $\theta_n$ of [lem-wf-finite-constant-h1-pi1] are additive. For a morphism of pointed schemes, reductions commute with precomposition on fundamental groups, and the $\theta_n$ commute with pullback by their naturality. Equality coordinatewise therefore proves the asserted naturality of the isomorphism.

Let $s$ be the degree-one lift in the Weil group of [def-wf-weil-group], and write $\alpha(g)=s^{-1}gs$ on $\Pi$. The explicit equivariance clause of [lem-wf-finite-constant-h1-pi1] states $\theta_n(\mathrm{Frob}(x_n))=\theta_n(x_n)\circ\alpha$. For the class associated with $b$, its right side is $(\rho_n\circ b)\circ\alpha=\rho_n\circ(b\circ\alpha)$. Thus in every coordinate the Frobenius transform of the class of $b$ is the class of $b\circ\alpha$. Equality of inverse-limit elements is coordinatewise equality, proving Frobenius equivariance and exactly the formula $b\mapsto[g\mapsto b(s^{-1}gs)]$ in the statement. No inverse convention is changed.

source.place: Proof, last sentence: explicit Weil-descent Frobenius action

The available Lean equivalence proves only the group-theoretic half.

lean.note: The comparison is an additive equivalence, natural for pointed morphisms via pullback of finite etale covers and fibre paths. Frobenius is the actual geometric Galois Frobenius pullback; its character action is explicitly inverse conjugation by a degree-one element of the recorded scheme Weil group. The existing curveH1CoefficientSystem applies to every scheme and is reused without any curve or smoothness hypothesis. Sheaf.H is the recorded Ext model of Etale.cohomology; no cohomology definition is replaced. Reviewer fix (cc review, 2026-10-18): the delivered helper padicH1FiberPullbackIso duplicated the existing AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.FiniteEtale.pullbackFiberIso (WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.FundamentalGroup.Restriction, the first projection on fibre points); it is removed and the Frobenius clause uses pullbackFiberIso p.geometricFiberProj x. padicH1FundamentalMap is kept: it equals Scheme.FiniteEtale.fundamentalGroupMap τ (Aut (fiber x)) (Aut (fiber y)), which needs a ConnectedSpace instance on the target that the theorem only has as explicit geometric-connectedness proofs. The upstream Scheme.EtaleTorsor.continuousMonoidHomPadicEquiv (and _comp), tagged for this item in blueprint main-20261017, is a plain bijection for a connected scheme into sheafHOneLimit, with an abstract transport hypothesis instead of the Weil-group formula and without additivity or pointed naturality, so it does not state the node and the module is needed.

statement_change.what: The local statement did not spell out the ambient finite base field and the chapter-wide convention that ℓ is a prime distinct from the base characteristic. The opening paragraph of sk-d-real-setup fixes ℓ ≠ p; omitting this binder would state a generalization beyond that source scope. The corrected statement makes those ambient assumptions explicit; no conclusion or proof route changes.

source.place: Opening paragraph: fixes q = p^a, k = algebraic closure of F_q, and a prime ℓ ≠ p; applied to equation (3.2) in lem-wf-additive-characters-h1.

citers.note: The rank-one theorem explicitly assumes ℓ does not divide q, so ℓ is distinct from the characteristic p of F_q. Its use of the Frobenius-equivariant comparison for scaled integral coordinate characters is unchanged.
